findings.finding: The proposed midpoint difference against alpha_terminal times the old unscaled terminal gradient is not self-justifying under repeated FP32 handoffs. Keep it only with a separately frozen terminal-residual FD guard at both widths. If that guard fails, do not report the midpoint component as passed; an actual alpha-scaled terminal-only chain may be run as a bounded diagnostic.

State explicitly that y=0 and sigma=1 are synthetic numeric residual settings, not observations or R. Freeze the exact h(q,Z), alpha values, arithmetic order, FP32 cast points, and all component-specific denominators before revealing any new residual FD values.

frozen_acceptance_recommendation.each_component: Predeclare <=1% FD/AD discrepancy at both widths, resolved signal using the frozen no-floor 100*eps64 scale, <=1% adjacent-width difference, and no >1% one-sided gap at both widths. Use separate component denominators; a full-objective pass must not hide a missing midpoint.
frozen_acceptance_recommendation.full: Compare dot(v, g_new_0_f32) to central FD of the complete two-residual J at actual transmitted FP32 eta +/-0.01 and +/-0.03.
frozen_acceptance_recommendation.midpoint: Compare dAD_mid to central FD of the midpoint residual term alone at the same two widths.
frozen_acceptance_recommendation.scaled_terminal_guard: Compare alpha_terminal*dot(v,g_old_terminal_0_f32) to central FD of the terminal residual term alone at the same widths.
frozen_acceptance_recommendation.trajectory_gate: Each new prefix must reproduce all N+1 packed FP64 states bytewise against the accepted baseline before its checked Fortran pullback; bind source, executable, input, namelist, protocol, eta, tolerances, and runtime evidence.

midpoint_increment_decision.interpretation: Call this the midpoint increment of the tested composite-chain gradient relative to the checked scaled terminal baseline; it is not a claim that finite-precision window composition is exactly additive. Require its own midpoint-residual FD comparison. If the scaled-terminal guard fails due to FP32 rescaling, stop acceptance; four additional lower terminal-only VJPs may diagnose that discrepancy but cannot erase a failed primary composite check.
midpoint_increment_decision.reason: This is a bounded, independently FD-checkable midpoint increment relative to the reused terminal-only baseline. The old terminal chain is for unscaled q_N, so FP32 handoff nonlinearity means alpha_terminal*g_old is not automatically identical to a newly run alpha-scaled terminal-only chain.
midpoint_increment_decision.required_guard: Before treating dAD_mid as an accepted component comparison, separately compare alpha_terminal*dot(v,g_old_terminal_0_f32) with the terminal residual FD contribution at both frozen widths, including signal, plateau, and one-sided checks. The old unscaled q_N check alone does not validate arbitrary FP32 cotangent rescaling.

negative_tests: Omit the midpoint cotangent while retaining the terminal term; the separate midpoint component check must fail even if the total discrepancy is small.
Use the wrong sign or omit the residual factor alpha=(h-y)/sigma^2; independent scalar residual derivatives and the component FD checks must reject it.

Change either frozen sigma or y after alpha/objective freeze; the protocol binding should reject the changed fixture, and a wrong-sigma or baseline-frozen-alpha synthetic calculation should fail the corresponding residual FD test.

objective.numeric_fixture: y_mid=y_terminal=0 and sigma_mid=sigma_terminal=1 are explicitly synthetic fixed scalar settings, not observations, measurement uncertainties, R, or a production observation cost.
objective.perturbed_FD: Recompute h_mid and h_terminal from each retained perturbed accepted state and evaluate the same frozen residual formula; do not freeze alpha at the baseline when evaluating perturbed J.

recommended_cotangent_and_chain.control: Keep the original post-initialization solver-entry control and old eta values; only the objective cotangents change.
recommended_cotangent_and_chain.precision: Compute baseline h and alpha in FP64 from the accepted FP64 states and frozen FP32 q vectors. Use FP64 for alpha scaling and cotangent addition, then one specified FP32 publication at each Fortran ABI handoff.

scope: Read-only preflight of the proposed two-time scalar residual objective and segmented native Fortran FP32 VJP plan. No new residual finite-difference results were inspected; no source, build, or model changes were made.
